levels.title: Money in One Level
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the three jobs money does: a way to pay, a measure of value and a way to save.

levels.title: Before Money: Barter
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how barter works and why it gets awkward.

levels.title: Shells, Salt and Stones
levels.objective: After this level you can describe early forms of money like cowrie shells and explain why they worked.

levels.title: The First Coins
levels.objective: After this level you can explain where the first coins came from and why metal made good money.

levels.title: Paper Money
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how paper money began in China and spread around the world.

levels.title: Why Money Has Value
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why money is valuable because people trust it and accept it.

levels.title: The Gold Standard
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what the gold standard was and why countries left it.

levels.title: Money as Numbers
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why most money today exists only as numbers in bank records.

levels.title: Cryptocurrency
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what cryptocurrencies are and how they differ from money in a bank.

levels.title: Checkpoint: What Money Is
levels.objective: After this level you can trace money from barter and coins to digital money, and explain what gives it value.

levels.title: Where Income Comes From
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the main ways people earn money: wages, profits, interest and rent.

levels.title: Gross and Net Pay
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why take-home pay is smaller than the salary on a job offer.

levels.title: Budgets
levels.objective: After this level you can build a simple budget that separates needs, wants and saving.

levels.title: Needs and Wants
levels.objective: After this level you can tell needs from wants and explain why the line differs from person to person.

levels.title: Opportunity Cost
levels.objective: After this level you can explain that every choice costs the next best thing you give up.

levels.title: How Prices Nudge You
levels.objective: After this level you can spot common pricing tricks like prices ending in 99 and decoy options.

levels.title: Paying by Card
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how a card payment works and who pays the fees.

levels.title: Small Costs Add Up
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how small recurring costs like subscriptions add up over a year.

levels.title: Scams and Fraud
levels.objective: After this level you can recognize common money scams and their warning signs.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Earning and Spending
levels.objective: After this level you can build a budget and explain how income, prices and ways of paying affect it.

levels.title: What Banks Do
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how banks take deposits and make loans.

levels.title: How Banks Create Money
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how bank lending creates most of the money in circulation.

levels.title: Interest
levels.objective: After this level you can explain interest as the price of borrowing money.

levels.title: Compound Interest
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how earning interest on interest makes money grow faster over time.

levels.title: Credit Cards and Debt
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how credit card interest can turn a small debt into a big one.

levels.title: Credit Scores
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what a credit score measures and what raises or lowers it.

levels.title: Mortgages
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how a mortgage works and why it lasts for decades.

levels.title: Loans for Big Goals
levels.objective: After this level you can compare loans for school, cars and businesses.

levels.title: When Banks Fail
levels.objective: After this level you can explain bank runs and how deposit insurance protects savers.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Banks and Borrowing
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how banks, interest and credit work together, and the risks of debt.

levels.title: Why Save?
levels.objective: After this level you can explain emergency funds and saving for goals.

levels.title: Risk and Return
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why higher possible returns come with higher risk.

levels.title: What a Stock Is
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what owning a share of a company means.

levels.title: What a Bond Is
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how a bond works as a loan to a government or company.

levels.title: Stock Markets
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how stock exchanges match buyers and sellers.

levels.title: Diversification
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why spreading money across many investments lowers risk.

levels.title: Index Funds
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what index funds are and why they are popular.

levels.title: Saving for Retirement
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why starting early matters so much when saving for retirement.

levels.title: Property and Other Assets
levels.objective: After this level you can describe property, commodities and the other things people invest in.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Saving and Investing
levels.objective: After this level you can compare saving, stocks, bonds and funds by risk and return.

levels.title: What a Market Is
levels.objective: After this level you can explain a market as any place where buyers and sellers meet.

levels.title: Supply
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why sellers offer more of something when its price rises.

levels.title: Demand
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why buyers want less of something when its price rises.

levels.title: Where Prices Come From
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how supply and demand together set a price.

levels.title: Shortages and Surpluses
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what happens when prices are held too low or too high.

levels.title: Competition
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how competition pushes prices down and quality up.

levels.title: Monopolies
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what a monopoly is and why governments limit them.

levels.title: Incentives
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how incentives shape the choices people make.

levels.title: Scarcity
levels.objective: After this level you can explain scarcity as the basic problem that economics studies.

levels.title: Milestone: How Markets Work
levels.objective: After this level you can connect money, banks, investing and markets into one picture of how an economy runs.

levels.title: Taxes
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what taxes pay for and name the main kinds of tax.

levels.title: Who Pays What
levels.objective: After this level you can compare tax systems where the rate rises with income to systems with one rate.

levels.title: Public Goods
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why things like roads and lighthouses are usually paid for by governments.

levels.title: Government Budgets and Debt
levels.objective: After this level you can explain deficits, surpluses and national debt.

levels.title: Central Banks
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what a central bank does and why it is kept independent.

levels.title: Interest Rates and the Economy
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how central banks raise or lower interest rates to cool or boost the economy.

levels.title: Printing Money
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why creating money too fast makes prices rise.

levels.title: Rules for Business
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why governments set rules for banks and businesses.

levels.title: Safety Nets
levels.objective: After this level you can explain unemployment insurance, pensions and other safety nets.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Governments and Money
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how taxes, spending and central banks shape an economy.

levels.title: What Inflation Is
levels.objective: After this level you can explain inflation as a general rise in prices over time.

levels.title: Measuring Inflation
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how a basket of everyday goods measures the cost of living.

levels.title: Hyperinflation
levels.objective: After this level you can describe hyperinflation in Weimar Germany and Zimbabwe and explain what caused it.

levels.title: Deflation
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why falling prices can hurt an economy.

levels.title: GDP
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what GDP measures and what it misses.

levels.title: The Business Cycle
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why economies go through booms and recessions.

levels.title: Unemployment
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how unemployment is measured and name its main causes.

levels.title: Bubbles
levels.objective: After this level you can explain speculative bubbles, from Dutch tulips to dot-com stocks.

levels.title: The Great Depression
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what caused the Great Depression and how it changed economic policy.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Booms and Busts
levels.objective: After this level you can connect inflation, bubbles and recessions, using the 2008 financial crisis as the example.

levels.title: Why Countries Trade
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why trade can leave both sides better off.

levels.title: Comparative Advantage
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why countries gain by specializing, even when one is better at everything.

levels.title: Imports and Exports
levels.objective: After this level you can explain imports, exports and the balance of trade.

levels.title: Tariffs
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what tariffs are and who ends up paying them.

levels.title: Exchange Rates
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how currencies are traded and why their values change.

levels.title: From Caravans to Containers
levels.objective: After this level you can trace how trade routes grew from the Silk Road to container ships.

levels.title: Globalization
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how supply chains stretch across many countries.

levels.title: Rich and Poor Countries
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the main reasons some countries are richer than others.

levels.title: Global Institutions
levels.objective: After this level you can describe what the IMF, the World Bank and the WTO do.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Trade and the Global Economy
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why countries trade and how tariffs and exchange rates affect it.

levels.title: What a Company Is
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how companies are owned and organized.

levels.title: Starting a Business
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what an entrepreneur does and what it costs to start a business.

levels.title: Revenue, Costs and Profit
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how a business makes a profit.

levels.title: Economies of Scale
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why making more of something can make each one cheaper.

levels.title: Division of Labor
levels.objective: After this level you can explain Adam Smith's pin factory and why specializing raises output.

levels.title: What Sets Wages
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what determines how much a job pays.

levels.title: Unions
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what unions are and how collective bargaining works.

levels.title: Automation and Jobs
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how machines have changed work, from looms to robots.

levels.title: Advertising
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how advertising shapes what people buy.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Companies and Work
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how businesses make profits, set wages and change with technology.

levels.title: Adam Smith and the Invisible Hand
levels.objective: After this level you can explain Smith's idea that self-interest can serve the common good through markets.

levels.title: Karl Marx and Capitalism's Critics
levels.objective: After this level you can explain Marx's critique of capitalism and how far it spread.

levels.title: Keynes and Spending in a Slump
levels.objective: After this level you can explain Keynes's argument for government spending during a slump.

levels.title: Markets, Plans and Mixed Economies
levels.objective: After this level you can compare market, planned and mixed economies.

levels.title: Behavioral Economics
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why real people don't always act rationally with money.

levels.title: Game Theory
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the prisoner's dilemma and why cooperation is hard.

levels.title: Inequality
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how income and wealth inequality are measured.

levels.title: Externalities
levels.objective: After this level you can explain costs like pollution that fall on people outside a deal.

levels.title: The Economics of Your Life
levels.objective: After this level you can apply the tree's big ideas to everyday choices about work, saving and spending.

levels.title: Mastery Challenge: How Money Works
levels.objective: After this level you can demonstrate command of How Money Works Levels 1–99 across the whole tree.
